from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear systems represent the intersection of lines.",
            "Two equations define two distinct paths.",
            "Their intersection point is the unique solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretation", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-4, 4], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")

        line1 = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x + 1, color=BLUE)
        line2 = axes.plot(lambda x: -1 * x - 0.5, color=RED)
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(axes.c2p(-1, 0.5))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(line1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(line2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Matrix: The 'Undo' Button", [
            "Inverse matrices act as undo buttons.",
            "Matrix A transforms a vector's position.",
            "Inverse A brings the vector home."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*1.0, buff=0, color=BLUE)
        matrix_a = MathTex("A = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\\\ 0 & 1 \\end{pmatrix}", color=YELLOW)
        inv_a = MathTex("A^{-1} = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\\\ 0 & 1 \\end{pmatrix}", color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(inv_a, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a), FadeIn(inv_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        point = Dot(self.grid["B5"], color=BLUE)
        label = Text("Vector v", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A5")
        self.play(FadeIn(point), FadeIn(label))
        
        # Transform animation: point moves
        new_pos = self.grid["B6"]
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(new_pos), label.animate.move_to(new_pos + UP*0.4))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        
        # Reverse animation: point returns
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]), label.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"] + UP*0.4))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Column space is the reach of transformation.",
            "It spans all possible reachable destinations.",
            "Visualize this as a reachable region."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Column Space: The Reach of a Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup 3D axes
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], z_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display column vectors in 3D
        vec1 = Vector([2, 1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        vec2 = Vector([0, 1, 2], color=BLUE)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.add(axes)
        self.play(Create(vec1), Create(vec2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Span the space covered
        plane = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0, 0, 0), 
            axes.c2p(2, 1, 0), 
            axes.c2p(2, 2, 2), 
            axes.c2p(0, 1, 2), 
            fill_opacity=0.3, color=GREEN
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Indicate output vectors lie within this span
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 1.5, 1), color=RED)
        label = Text("Reachable", font_size=16, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A6")
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Null space collapses vectors to zero.", "It acts as a ghost zone.", "Everything here becomes invisible to transformation."]
        self.setup_layout("Null Space: The 'Ghost' Zone", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        dot = Dot(color=BLUE)
        origin = Dot(color=RED)
        line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color=YELLOW)
        area = Rectangle(width=4, height=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), FadeIn(origin))
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(origin, 'C5')
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(origin.get_center()))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'D3')
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_in_area(area, 'D2', 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.play(FadeOut(dot), FadeOut(line))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Invertible matrices span the whole space.", 
            "Singular matrices collapse dimensions into lines.", 
            "Algebra connects deeply with geometric intuition."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        eq = MathTex("A\\mathbf{x} = \\mathbf{b} \\implies \\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\\mathbf{b}").set_color(BLUE)
        concepts = VGroup(
            Text("Determinant = 0", font_size=24, color=YELLOW),
            Text("Null Space > {0}", font_size=24, color=RED),
            Text("Collapsed Geometry", font_size=24, color=ORANGE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        connection = VGroup(
            Text("Algebraic", font_size=24, color=BLUE),
            Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).set_height(0.5),
            Text("Geometric", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.place_in_area(concepts, 'D1', 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(concepts))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(connection, 'C5')
        self.play(FadeIn(connection))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Linear Systems & Fundamental Subspaces: A Visual Journey

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation: The Intersection of Worlds
sections.content: Introduce linear systems as the intersection of lines/planes. Use a 2D coordinate system where two linear equations represent two lines. Emphasize that the solution is the point where they cross (or the line if they are identical).
sections.example: Visualizing two paths of 'Robot A' and 'Robot B'; where their paths cross is the unique solution coordinate (x, y).

sections.title: The Inverse Matrix: The 'Undo' Button
sections.content: Explain the inverse matrix as the transformation that reverses a linear operation. If matrix A maps a vector to a new position, A⁻¹ maps it back to the origin state. Prerequisite: Understanding matrix-vector multiplication as a transformation.
sections.example: A 'Spatial Teleporter' device: Matrix A moves a cat from Point A to Point B; the inverse matrix A⁻¹ acts as the 'Return Home' button to bring the cat back.

sections.title: Column Space: The Reach of a Transformation
sections.content: Define column space as the span of the column vectors. It represents all possible destinations (output space) reachable by the matrix transformation. Visualize this as a 'reachable region' on the 2D/3D plane.
sections.example: A 'Paint Brush' robot: The column space represents the total area on the canvas the robot can cover given its two mechanical arm vectors.

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Zone
sections.content: Define null space as the set of vectors that the matrix collapses to the zero vector. Visualize this as the 'Kernel'—what gets 'deleted' or flattened by the transformation.
sections.example: A 'Magic Lens': Anything placed inside the null space zone of the lens becomes invisible (mapped to zero) when viewed through the lens.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Connect the concepts: If a matrix has an inverse, the column space spans the whole room and the null space contains only the origin point. Review the interplay between geometry and algebra.
sections.example: A 'Dimensional Map': A square matrix is like a complete map (invertible); a singular matrix is like a map folded flat into a line (losing information in the null space).
